counties.name: Mombasa
counties.history: Mombasa is Kenya's oldest city and main port. It has been a major trading hub since the 9th century, attracting Arab, Persian, and Portuguese traders. Fort Jesus, built by the Portuguese in 1593, stands as a testament to this rich history.
counties.funFact: Mombasa is the only county in Kenya that is entirely an island city connected to the mainland by causeways and ferries.
counties.climate: Hot and humid tropical climate with temperatures ranging 22–33°C. Two rainy seasons: April–June and October–November.
counties.roadNetwork: A109 Mombasa–Nairobi Highway, Makupa Causeway, Likoni Ferry

counties.name: Kwale
counties.history: Kwale County, formerly part of the Coast Province, is renowned for its pristine beaches and rich Mijikenda culture. The Shimba Hills harbor some of Kenya's most diverse wildlife.
counties.funFact: Kwale is home to the largest sable antelope population in East Africa within Shimba Hills.
counties.climate: Tropical with coastal humidity. Rainfall 800–1200mm annually.
counties.roadNetwork: B8 South Coast Road, C106 Kwale–Kinango Road

counties.name: Kilifi
counties.history: Kilifi is home to ancient ruins including the Gede Ruins, a medieval Swahili town that flourished from the 13th to 17th centuries. The county has one of the richest coastlines in Kenya.
counties.funFact: The Arabuko-Sokoke Forest in Kilifi is one of the largest remaining coastal forests in East Africa and home to rare species like the golden-rumped elephant shrew.
counties.climate: Hot tropical coast climate. Annual rainfall 900–1500mm.
counties.roadNetwork: A7 Mombasa–Malindi Road, B8 Kilifi–Mariakani Road

counties.name: Tana River
counties.history: Tana River County is named after Kenya's longest river, the Tana. The county is sparsely populated and has been historically affected by inter-ethnic conflicts between the Orma and Pokomo communities.
counties.funFact: Tana River County is home to two critically endangered primate species: the Tana River Red Colobus and the Tana River Mangabey.
counties.climate: Semi-arid to arid. Low and erratic rainfall 200–500mm.
counties.roadNetwork: C112 Garsen–Hola Road

counties.name: Lamu
counties.history: Lamu Old Town is Kenya's oldest living town and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. It has been a centre of Islamic culture and Swahili civilization for over 700 years.
counties.funFact: Lamu Old Town is one of the best-preserved Swahili settlements in East Africa and has no cars — donkeys are the main mode of transport!
counties.climate: Hot and humid tropical. Northeast monsoon November–March; Southeast monsoon April–October.
counties.roadNetwork: Ferry access; limited road network on mainland

counties.name: Taita-Taveta
counties.history: Taita-Taveta is home to the Taita Hills, one of Africa's biodiversity hotspots. The county hosts the largest national park complex in Kenya — Tsavo East and West.
counties.funFact: Lake Chala, on the Kenya-Tanzania border in Taita-Taveta, is a volcanic crater lake with crystal-clear water reaching 92m depth.
counties.climate: Semi-arid with rainfall 250–750mm. Cooler in the Taita Hills.
counties.roadNetwork: A109 Nairobi–Mombasa Highway passes through Voi

counties.name: Garissa
counties.history: Garissa is the largest county by area in the former North Eastern Province. It borders Somalia and has strong Somali cultural ties. The county gained tragic notoriety in 2015 with the Garissa University attack.
counties.funFact: Garissa County is one of the fastest-growing counties in Kenya due to urbanization and the establishment of Garissa University.
counties.climate: Arid and semi-arid. Rainfall below 300mm per year.
counties.roadNetwork: A3 Nairobi–Garissa Highway

counties.name: Wajir
counties.history: Wajir is one of Kenya's most remote counties, covering vast arid semi-desert. It was part of the Northern Frontier District during British colonial rule and has strong Somali pastoral heritage.
counties.funFact: Wajir County has one of the lowest population densities in Kenya despite being the second largest county by area.
counties.climate: Extremely arid. Rainfall 150–300mm per year. Temperatures up to 40°C.
counties.roadNetwork: B9 Garissa–Wajir–Mandera Road

counties.name: Mandera
counties.history: Mandera sits at the junction of Kenya, Ethiopia, and Somalia — the Mandera Triangle. It is Kenya's most northeasterly county with a predominantly Somali population and strong trade links to neighboring countries.
counties.funFact: From Mandera town, you can see three countries — Kenya, Somalia, and Ethiopia — simultaneously!
counties.climate: Hot and very dry. Temperatures average 30–40°C. Rainfall under 200mm.
counties.roadNetwork: B9 Road connecting to Wajir and Garissa

counties.name: Marsabit
counties.history: Marsabit is Kenya's largest county. It contains the northern shores of Lake Turkana — a UNESCO World Heritage Site and home to the Jade Sea, the world's largest desert lake.
counties.funFact: Marsabit is the largest county in Kenya at over 70,000 km², larger than some countries!
counties.climate: Arid. Marsabit town is cool due to altitude. Chalbi Desert is one of the hottest areas.
counties.roadNetwork: A2 Nairobi–Marsabit–Moyale Highway (Ethiopia border)

counties.name: Isiolo
counties.history: Isiolo is the gateway to northern Kenya. Originally a World War I settlement, it grew into a major town and transit hub. It sits at the crossroads where highland and arid environments meet.
counties.funFact: Isiolo is often called the 'Gateway to Northern Kenya' — north of this town, you're entering a vast, untamed frontier.
counties.climate: Semi-arid to arid transitional zone. Rainfall 200–500mm.
counties.roadNetwork: A2 Nanyuki–Isiolo–Moyale Highway

counties.name: Meru
counties.history: Meru County is on the northeastern slopes of Mount Kenya. Famous for miraa (khat), tea, and coffee. The Meru people have a rich oral tradition and were among the first to be evangelized by Methodist missionaries.
counties.funFact: Meru County produces over 80% of Kenya's miraa (khat), exported globally including to Somalia, Yemen, and the UK.
counties.climate: Temperate on highlands, warmer in lower areas. Rainfall 1000–1700mm.
counties.roadNetwork: B6 Nairobi–Meru Highway, A2 Meru–Isiolo Road

counties.name: Tharaka-Nithi
counties.history: Tharaka-Nithi is one of Kenya's smallest counties, carved out of the former Eastern Province. The Tharaka people are known for their unique cultural practices including traditional hunting.
counties.funFact: The name Tharaka-Nithi comes from two rivers: the Tharaka lowlands and the Nithi River that flows through the county.
counties.climate: Temperate in highlands; hot and dry in Tharaka lowlands.
counties.roadNetwork: B6 Nairobi–Chuka Road

counties.name: Embu
counties.history: Embu County lies on the southeastern slopes of Mount Kenya. The Embu people are closely related to the Kikuyu and Meru, and historically farmed the fertile mountain slopes.
counties.funFact: The iconic Tana River — Kenya's longest river — originates from the glaciers of Mount Kenya in Embu County.
counties.climate: Cool and wet on Mount Kenya slopes. Rainfall 1000–1800mm.
counties.roadNetwork: B6 Nairobi–Embu Road, A3 Embu–Garissa Road

counties.name: Kitui
counties.history: Kitui County is the homeland of the Kamba people. George Adamson, the conservationist immortalized in 'Born Free', worked at Kora National Reserve in Kitui until his death in 1989.
counties.funFact: The Mui Basin in Kitui holds one of Africa's largest coal deposits, potentially transforming Kenya's energy landscape.
counties.climate: Semi-arid. Bimodal rainfall 500–1000mm. Hot and dry.
counties.roadNetwork: A3 Nairobi–Kitui–Garissa Highway

counties.name: Machakos
counties.history: Machakos was Kenya's first administrative capital under British rule. The Kamba people of Machakos are famed for their craftsmanship, particularly woodcarving. The county is also known as 'Macha Vegas'.
counties.funFact: Machakos was the first administrative capital of Kenya during British colonial rule, before Nairobi took over in 1901.
counties.climate: Semi-arid highlands. Bimodal rainfall 600–1000mm.
counties.roadNetwork: A109 Nairobi–Mombasa Highway, A3 Machakos–Kitui Road

counties.name: Makueni
counties.history: Makueni County is part of the Kamba homeland. Known for innovative governance, it runs a free healthcare system. The county is emerging as a mango production hub for Kenya and the region.
counties.funFact: Makueni produces some of the best mangoes in Kenya and is pioneering a mango processing factory that helps farmers access global markets.
counties.climate: Semi-arid to arid. Rainfall 400–900mm.
counties.roadNetwork: A109 Nairobi–Mombasa Highway passes through Kibwezi

counties.name: Nyandarua
counties.history: Nyandarua was the heartland of the Mau Mau forest fighters during Kenya's independence struggle. The Aberdare Mountains are named after Lord Aberdare, a British politician.
counties.funFact: Nyandarua County has the highest pyrethrum production in Kenya — the flower is used as a natural insecticide worldwide.
counties.climate: Cold and wet. Rainfall 1000–2000mm. Frost common at high altitudes.
counties.roadNetwork: B5 Nairobi–Ol Kalou Road, C72 Ndaragua Road

counties.name: Nyeri
counties.history: Nyeri is where Princess Elizabeth became Queen in 1952 at Treetops Lodge. It is also where Lord Baden-Powell, founder of the Boy Scout movement, is buried.
counties.funFact: Queen Elizabeth II learned of her father King George VI's death — and thus became Queen — while staying at Treetops Lodge in Nyeri in 1952!
counties.climate: Cool and wet. Rainfall 1000–2000mm. Temperature 10–25°C.
counties.roadNetwork: B5 Nairobi–Nyeri–Nanyuki Highway

counties.name: Kirinyaga
counties.history: Kirinyaga County is named after Mount Kenya (Kirinyaga in Kikuyu, meaning 'Mountain of Whiteness'). It is one of Kenya's richest agricultural counties, known for premium Kirinyaga tea and coffee.
counties.funFact: The Mwea rice irrigation scheme in Kirinyaga is the largest rice growing region in Kenya, supplying much of the country's local rice.
counties.climate: Temperate in highlands. Rainfall 1000–2000mm.
counties.roadNetwork: B6 Nairobi–Kerugoya Road

counties.name: Murang'a
counties.history: Murang'a (formerly Fort Hall) was a major Mau Mau resistance base during the liberation struggle. The county's Kenol-Muranga area is famous for commercial horticulture destined for European markets.
counties.funFact: Murang'a County is one of the biggest producers of avocados in Kenya, exported globally for the avocado oil and food industry.
counties.climate: Temperate to cool. Rainfall 1000–2000mm.
counties.roadNetwork: A2 Nairobi–Murang'a–Nyeri Highway

counties.name: Kiambu
counties.history: Kiambu is the most populous county outside of Nairobi and forms the suburban belt of the capital. It is one of Kenya's most economically productive counties, known for premium tea estates.
counties.funFact: Kiambu County has the highest number of millionaires per capita in Kenya outside Nairobi, driven by real estate and tea industry wealth.
universities: Jomo Kenyatta University of Agriculture & Technology (JKUAT)
counties.climate: Temperate. Rainfall 1000–1800mm.
counties.roadNetwork: A2 Nairobi–Thika Superhighway, Northern Bypass

counties.name: Turkana
counties.history: Turkana County borders South Sudan, Uganda, and Ethiopia. Lake Turkana, the world's largest permanent desert lake, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and 'Cradle of Mankind' — some of humanity's oldest fossils were found here.
counties.funFact: Lake Turkana's southern island, Central Island, is home to the world's largest Nile crocodile breeding ground.
counties.climate: Extremely hot and arid. Temperatures up to 42°C. Annual rainfall under 200mm.
counties.roadNetwork: A1 Kitale–Lodwar Road

counties.name: West Pokot
counties.history: West Pokot is home to the Pokot people, famed for their age-set system, cattle culture, and distinctive adornment. The county borders Uganda and has significant cattle-rustling challenges.
counties.funFact: Kapenguria, the county capital, was where Jomo Kenyatta was detained and tried by the British colonial government in 1952–1953.
counties.climate: Semi-arid lowlands; cool in Cherangani Hills. Rainfall 500–1200mm.
counties.roadNetwork: A1 Kitale–Kapenguria Road

counties.name: Samburu
counties.history: The Samburu are a Nilotic people closely related to the Maasai, known as 'The Butterfly People' for their colorful attire and beadwork. Maralal is famous for hosting one of Africa's most unique camel races.
counties.funFact: The Maralal International Camel Derby in Samburu is the only camel racing event in East Africa, drawing international participants every year.
counties.climate: Semi-arid to arid. Rainfall 250–600mm.
counties.roadNetwork: C77 Nyahururu–Maralal Road

counties.name: Trans-Nzoia
counties.history: Trans-Nzoia is Kenya's maize basket. Kitale became a European settlement in the early 1900s and developed as an agricultural hub. The county borders Uganda at Mount Elgon.
counties.funFact: Trans-Nzoia County is Kenya's leading maize producer — it's often called the 'Breadbasket of Kenya'.
counties.climate: Temperate. Moderate rainfall 1200–1800mm. Very fertile.
counties.roadNetwork: A1 Eldoret–Kitale Road, B2 Kitale–Kapenguria

counties.name: Uasin Gishu
counties.history: Uasin Gishu is Kenya's athletics capital. Eldoret has produced more Olympic champions than any city of its size on earth. Runners like Eliud Kipchoge, the greatest marathon runner ever, hail from this region.
counties.funFact: Eldoret is called the 'City of Champions' — more Olympic and World Championship gold medals have been won per capita by athletes from here than anywhere else on Earth.
counties.climate: Cool and temperate. Altitude ~2100m. Rainfall 900–1500mm.
counties.roadNetwork: A104 Nairobi–Eldoret Highway, A1 Eldoret–Kitale Road

counties.name: Elgeyo-Marakwet
counties.history: Elgeyo-Marakwet is home to Iten — dubbed the 'Home of Champions'. The Kerio Valley is a spectacular escarpment that provides a dramatic training environment for world-class athletes.
counties.funFact: Iten town, the county capital, is internationally known as the 'Home of Champions' and attracts athletes from over 60 countries to train at altitude.
counties.climate: Cool at high altitude, hot in Kerio Valley. Rainfall 600–1500mm.
counties.roadNetwork: B56 Eldoret–Iten–Kabarnet Road

counties.name: Nandi
counties.history: The Nandi people fiercely resisted British colonial rule, with Koitalel Arap Samoei leading the Nandi Resistance for over a decade. The Nandi are among Kenya's top athletics producers.
counties.funFact: Koitalel Arap Samoei, the legendary Nandi chief who resisted British colonization for 10 years, was treacherously killed under the guise of peace negotiations in 1905.
counties.climate: Cool and wet highlands. Rainfall 1200–1800mm.
counties.roadNetwork: A104 Nakuru–Eldoret Road, B32 Kapsabet–Kisumu Road

counties.name: Baringo
counties.history: Baringo County is home to Lake Baringo and Lake Bogoria, two of the Rift Valley lakes. Lake Bogoria is a Ramsar wetland famous for its flamingo population and hot springs.
counties.funFact: Lake Bogoria in Baringo is home to the largest single congregation of flamingos in the world — up to 2 million birds at peak season.
counties.climate: Semi-arid lowlands; cool in Tugen Hills. Rainfall 500–1200mm.
counties.roadNetwork: B56 Nakuru–Kabarnet Road

counties.name: Laikipia
counties.history: Laikipia Plateau is one of Kenya's most important wildlife areas outside national parks. Ol Pejeta Conservancy houses the last two northern white rhinos on Earth.
counties.funFact: Ol Pejeta Conservancy in Laikipia is home to Najin and Fatu, the last two northern white rhinos in existence, kept under 24-hour armed guard.
counties.climate: Cool and semi-arid plateau. Rainfall 500–1000mm.
counties.roadNetwork: A2 Nairobi–Nanyuki Road, B5 Nyahururu–Nanyuki Road

counties.name: Nakuru
counties.history: Nakuru is Kenya's fourth largest city and an industrial hub. Lake Nakuru was once world-famous for its flamingos, though population has declined. Hell's Gate was the inspiration for Disney's Pride Rock in The Lion King.
counties.funFact: Hell's Gate National Park in Nakuru inspired the landscape of The Lion King, with the Maasai Mara savanna also contributing to the movie's visual design.
counties.climate: Temperate to warm. Rainfall 700–1200mm. Located in the Rift Valley.
counties.roadNetwork: A104 Nairobi–Nakuru–Eldoret Highway

counties.name: Narok
counties.history: Narok County is home to the Maasai Mara, one of the world's greatest wildlife spectacles. The Maasai people have lived in harmony with wildlife for centuries, making them iconic symbols of Kenya.
counties.funFact: The Maasai Mara hosts the Great Wildebeest Migration — over 1.5 million wildebeest, 500,000 zebras and 200,000 gazelles cross the Mara River annually in the world's greatest wildlife show.
counties.climate: Warm savanna with cool mornings. Rainfall 700–1200mm.
counties.roadNetwork: B3 Nairobi–Narok Road, C12 Narok–Sekenani Road

counties.name: Kajiado
counties.history: Kajiado is Maasai heartland with stunning views of Mount Kilimanjaro from Amboseli. Olorgesailie is a prehistoric site where Homo erectus tools dating back 700,000 years were found.
counties.funFact: From Amboseli National Park in Kajiado, you can photograph elephants with Mount Kilimanjaro as the backdrop — one of Africa's most iconic images.
counties.climate: Semi-arid. Hot and dry. Rainfall 300–700mm.
counties.roadNetwork: A104 Nairobi–Namanga Road, B8 Kajiado–Magadi Road

counties.name: Kericho
counties.history: Kericho is Kenya's tea capital, home to some of the world's finest tea estates. The county's climate — afternoon rainfall, volcanic soil, and altitude — creates perfect tea growing conditions.
counties.funFact: Kericho County produces approximately 15% of the world's black tea. Tea estates here are so large they're visible from satellite images!
counties.climate: Cool and very wet. Annual rainfall 1600–2200mm, very reliable.
counties.roadNetwork: A1 Nakuru–Kericho–Kisumu Road

counties.name: Bomet
counties.history: Bomet County is in the heart of Kipsigis territory, known for its tea production and athletics. The county was carved from Kericho and continues its agricultural heritage.
counties.funFact: Bomet County is one of Kenya's top tea and coffee exporting counties by volume, yet it remains one of the least urbanized.
counties.climate: Cool and wet. Rainfall 1200–1800mm.
counties.roadNetwork: B1 Nakuru–Kisii Road, C23 Bomet–Narok Road

counties.name: Kakamega
counties.history: Kakamega Forest is East Africa's only remaining equatorial rainforest and is estimated to be over 5 million years old. The county's Luhya people have a rich tradition of isukuti music and wrestling.
counties.funFact: Kakamega Forest is a fragment of the ancient Central African rainforest and contains plants and animals found nowhere else in East Africa.
universities: Masinde Muliro University of Science and Technology
counties.climate: Tropical humid. Heavy rainfall 1700–2200mm.
counties.roadNetwork: A1 Kisumu–Kakamega–Eldoret Road

counties.name: Vihiga
counties.history: Vihiga is Kenya's smallest county by area but one of its most densely populated. The Maragoli sub-tribe of the Luhya are known for their strong community bonds, education emphasis, and diaspora.
counties.funFact: Vihiga County is one of the most densely populated counties in Kenya, with over 1,000 people per square kilometer in some areas.
counties.climate: Tropical, humid. Rainfall 1500–2000mm.
counties.roadNetwork: A1 Kisumu–Kakamega Road, B5 Vihiga–Mbale Road

counties.name: Bungoma
counties.history: Bungoma County borders Uganda and is home to the Bukusu people. The county fought significant battles with colonizers, commemorated at Chetambe's Fort. Mount Elgon is an ancient extinct volcano.
counties.funFact: Mount Elgon, straddling Kenya and Uganda on Bungoma's border, is the oldest and largest extinct volcano in East Africa, at around 24 million years old.
counties.climate: Temperate and wet. Rainfall 1400–2000mm.
counties.roadNetwork: A104 Eldoret–Bungoma Road, A1 Bungoma–Kitale Road

counties.name: Busia
counties.history: Busia County sits on the Kenya-Uganda border, making it a major cross-border trade hub. The Busia border post is one of the busiest in East Africa for goods transit between Kenya and Uganda.
counties.funFact: The Busia border between Kenya and Uganda is one of the busiest land borders in East Africa, handling goods worth hundreds of millions of dollars annually.
counties.climate: Hot and humid. Rainfall 1200–1800mm.
counties.roadNetwork: A1 Kisumu–Busia–Uganda Road

counties.name: Siaya
counties.history: Siaya County is the ancestral home of the Luo people and of Barack Obama's father, Barack Obama Sr. The county has produced many of Kenya's leading intellectuals, politicians, and civil society leaders.
counties.funFact: Kogelo village in Siaya County is the ancestral home of Barack Obama, the 44th President of the United States, whose father was from here.
counties.climate: Tropical lakeside. Hot and humid. Rainfall 1000–1800mm.
counties.roadNetwork: B1 Kisumu–Bondo Road, C24 Siaya–Ugunja Road

counties.name: Kisumu
counties.history: Kisumu is Kenya's third largest city and the main port on Lake Victoria. Founded in 1901 as the terminus of the Uganda Railway, it grew into a commercial hub for the Lake Victoria region.
counties.funFact: Kisumu is one of the largest inland freshwater ports in the world, positioned on Lake Victoria — Africa's largest lake.
hospitals: Jaramogi Oginga Odinga Teaching & Referral Hospital
counties.climate: Hot and humid lakeside. Rainfall 1200–1800mm.
counties.roadNetwork: A1 Nairobi–Kisumu Road, B1 Kisumu–Busia Road

counties.name: Homa Bay
counties.history: Homa Bay County has a spectacular Lake Victoria shoreline. Thimlich Ohinga, a UNESCO World Heritage Site in the county, is a dry stone-walled structure built by Bantu settlers in the 16th century.
counties.funFact: Thimlich Ohinga in Homa Bay is a UNESCO World Heritage Site — a remarkable dry-stone walled complex that is the largest and best preserved of its kind in East Africa.
hospitals: Homa Bay County Teaching & Referral Hospital
counties.climate: Hot and humid. Lake Victoria influence. Rainfall 1000–1600mm.
counties.roadNetwork: B1 Kisumu–Homa Bay Road, C19 Homa Bay–Migori Road

counties.name: Migori
counties.history: Migori borders Tanzania and has strong cross-border trade ties. Gold mining is central to the local economy, and artisanal miners have worked the area for generations. The Kuria people straddle the Kenya-Tanzania border.
counties.funFact: Migori County is one of Kenya's top gold-producing regions, with artisanal miners extracting gold near the Tanzania border using traditional methods.
counties.climate: Tropical. Hot with moderate rainfall 1000–1500mm.
counties.roadNetwork: A1 Kisumu–Isebania–Tanzania Road, B1 Migori–Homa Bay Road

counties.name: Kisii
counties.history: Kisii County is home to the Gusii (Kisii) people, famous for their soapstone carvings exported worldwide. The county is densely populated and lies in one of Kenya's most fertile highlands.
counties.funFact: Kisii soapstone carvings are among Kenya's most recognizable export handicrafts, sold in markets worldwide from New York to Tokyo.
counties.climate: Cool and wet highland. Rainfall 1500–2000mm.
counties.roadNetwork: A1 Kisumu–Kisii–Nairobi Road, B1 Kisii–Homa Bay Road

counties.name: Nyamira
counties.history: Nyamira County was carved from Kisii County in 2013. It is one of Kenya's smallest counties and shares the Gusii culture. The Manga Ridge forms a scenic highland backdrop.
counties.funFact: Nyamira County is one of Kenya's youngest counties, having been created from Kisii County in 2013 when Kenya transitioned to a devolved system of government.
counties.climate: Cool and wet. Rainfall 1400–2000mm.
counties.roadNetwork: B1 Kisii–Nyamira Road

counties.name: Nairobi
counties.history: Nairobi is East Africa's largest city and Kenya's capital. It began as a railway camp in 1899 and grew into a global hub. It is the only capital city in the world with a national park within its boundaries.
counties.funFact: Nairobi National Park, just minutes from the city center, is the only national park in the world within a capital city — lions, rhinos, and giraffes roam against a skyline backdrop.
counties.climate: Pleasant highland climate. Temperature 13–25°C. Rainfall 600–1200mm.
counties.roadNetwork: Hub of Kenya's road network; Thika Superhighway, Southern Bypass, Eastern Bypass, Northern Bypass
